expected_mechanism: solver_fail immediately sets ok=False; switch to LQR occurs within one supervisor period (50 ms). LQR starts from non-zero error with clipped initial command.
MPC solver failure triggers immediate LQR handover. Error state at switch depends on how long MPC has been diverging before failure detection.
Prolonged solver failure may exhaust valid command fallback or trigger supervisor latch. LQR must recover from large lateral error.
Extended stale output delays LQR awareness of true vehicle state. By the time LQR takes over, error may have grown beyond linear model bounds.
Command delayed by 2 ticks (100 ms). Switch occurs at same cycle; LQR receives stale command one period late. Initial LQR correction may be offset but error state unchanged.
6-tick delay (300 ms) allows error to grow significantly before LQR takeover. At 40 km/h, lateral error accumulates; LQR may start from beyond its design point.
Bias added to steering output. LQR sees clipped command if bias pushes command beyond max_steer_rad. Recovery depends on sign of bias relative to current turn.
Large bias (0.1 rad) at high speed on curve exit. Command likely saturated at max_steer_rad. LQR switch occurs with command already at limit; recovery improbable without error reduction.
Fast drift (0.05 rad/s) will quickly saturate steering rate limit. At switch moment, LQR command is at rate limit; recovery requires error to decrease faster than integral action can unwind.
Steering saturated at positive max for 0.3s. LQR switch occurs with output at limit. Small error at 15 km/h may still allow recovery if error is within LQR's small-error assumption.
Steering held at negative max for 1.0s. At 40 km/h on curve exit, vehicle may have significant lateral error. LQR starts from saturated command and large error; recovery unlikely.
Intermittent bias turns on for 0.2s every 1.2s. Switch may occur during 'off' period when bias is zero, yielding clean LQR takeover; or during 'on' period with clipped command.
